problem_statement: StartBootstrap/startbootstrap-modern-business (rebranded here as the field-kit rental co-op Larkspur & Vane) is a Pug + SCSS + vanilla-JS Bootstrap 5 multi-page marketing template that builds a static site to dist/ (Home, About, Contact, Pricing, FAQ, Blog, Portfolio) sharing one navbar and footer. The Pricing page carries the site's core commercial control: a billing cadence toggle (Monthly / Annual) that rewrites the three plan cards (Free, Pro, Enterprise) and a 'Billing:' readout when the visitor switches cadence, plus a shared 'rental plan summary' rail that recaps the plans on the Home, Pricing, and FAQ pages. A recent change to the pricing system introduced three regressions. (1) On a 390px phone the shared plan rail's metric tiles are pinned to a fixed 720px non-wrapping row, so the page scrolls sideways. (2) The billing toggle's active pill still moves when clicked, but the plan prices and the 'Billing:' readout are frozen on the values rendered at page load, so choosing Annual never updates the prices or the readout. (3) The plan cards on the Pricing page collide: a tightened grid rule pulls each card on top of the previous one so the Free / Pro / Enterprise cards shingle and their prices and feature lists overlap and become illegible. Additionally the shared plan rail was only re-wired onto some routes, so it is missing from pages that used to show it. Repair the pricing system so that: the shared plan rail fits a 390px viewport with no horizontal overflow while staying intact on tablet and desktop; the billing toggle live-updates the plan prices and the 'Billing:' readout every time the cadence changes; the Pricing plan cards lay out cleanly side by side without overlapping or clipping; and the shared plan rail appears on the Home, Pricing, and FAQ pages. Leave all copy, section content, DOM structure, the contact form, the navbar, and the footer unchanged across every page.
required_content: The Pricing page billing toggle live-updates the Free/Pro/Enterprise prices and the 'Billing:' readout each time the visitor switches between Monthly and Annual (Annual shows the yearly price and 'Billing: Annual').

On a 390px mobile viewport no page has horizontal overflow beyond a small tolerance: the shared plan-rail tile row wraps or reflows to fit the screen instead of forcing the document wider than the viewport.
On desktop (1440px) the three pricing plan cards lay out cleanly side by side with no overlap, no clipping, and no visual regression; text in every card stays legible.
The shared 'rental plan summary' rail is present on the Home, Pricing, and FAQ pages with identical tiles and copy.

The shared navbar and footer, the Home hero, the Contact form and contact cards, the three pricing tiers, the FAQ accordion, and the Portfolio overview all remain present and unchanged in content and structure across their pages. No new console errors or failed network requests are introduced.

The shared 'rental plan summary' rail is the include `src/pug/includes/planrail.pug` whose root element carries the class `planrail`; keep this class and its existing metric-tile copy (including the 'Every kit, insured' tile) intact, and render the rail (class `planrail`) on the Home, Pricing, and FAQ pages.
design_constraints: Preserve the Modern Business design language: blue primary accent, Bootstrap card rhythm, shared dark navbar and footer, and the existing multi-page navigation.

Fix ONLY the pricing-system regressions (mobile overflow of the plan rail, the stale billing toggle, the overlapping plan cards, and the missing rail on some routes); do not rewrite copy, restructure sections, add or remove images, or change the navigation.

The layout repairs must live in the lever's own SCSS (src/scss/_planlever.scss) and its wiring in src/js/plan-billing.js and the shared rail include; they must not depend on hiding overflow at the body/html level or clipping content off-screen.
The plan rail must fit 390px mobile, 834px tablet, and 1440px desktop viewports; all four rail tiles and all three plan cards must remain readable at every size.
Keep the Pug/SCSS/JS build pipeline intact - `npm run build` must still emit a working static dist/.

Do not rename the shared plan rail's class `planrail` or rewrite its tile copy ('Every kit, insured' etc.); the rail markup and copy must stay byte-identical while you repair the wrapping/toggle/card layout.
state_constraints: desktop_pricing_default captures the Pricing page at 1440px: the billing toggle reads 'Billing: Monthly', the three plan cards lay out side by side with no overlap, and the shared plan rail is present.
desktop_pricing_annual clicks the Annual pill; the plan prices switch to the yearly figures ($86 Pro) and the readout reads 'Billing: Annual'.
mobile_pricing_default captures the Pricing page at 390px with no horizontal overflow and legible, non-overlapping plan cards.
mobile_home and tablet_home confirm the shared plan rail fits the viewport with no horizontal overflow.
desktop_faq and mobile_faq confirm the shared plan rail is present on the FAQ page.
desktop_contact and desktop_portfolio confirm the contact form and portfolio overview remain intact across the multi-page flow.

change_completion: The billing toggle live-updates the plan prices and the 'Billing:' readout on every cadence change.
The mobile pages no longer overflow horizontally: the shared plan-rail tile row reflows to fit a 390px viewport.
The three pricing plan cards lay out cleanly side by side without overlapping or clipping.
design_consistency: The repair preserves the Modern Business Bootstrap identity, page order, and all surrounding content.
The shared plan rail appears on Home, Pricing, and FAQ with identical tiles and copy.
responsive: At 390px the shared plan-rail tile row wraps or flexes down so the document width stays within the viewport.
At 834px and 1440px the plan rail and the plan cards lay out cleanly with no horizontal overflow.
regression: Navbar, footer, Home hero, contact form, pricing tiers, FAQ, and Portfolio remain present and unchanged.
No new console errors or failed network requests appear on any captured state.

author_notes: Repo-grounded repair on the static StartBootstrap Modern Business multi-page template (Pug/SCSS/JS -> dist/), rebranded Larkspur & Vane field-kit rentals. The native lever is the Pricing page's billing cadence toggle (Monthly/Annual) plus a shared rental-plan rail. The seeded defects are four orthogonal regressions: a mobile horizontal-overflow of the plan-rail tile row (fixed 720px non-wrapping), a stale billing toggle whose prices and 'Billing:' readout are snapshotted at load and never re-read, collided/shingled pricing plan cards pulled on top of each other by a negative-margin grid rule, and the shared rail missing from the FAQ route. The reference repair lets the rail row wrap (flex-wrap:wrap + flex:1 1 150px), re-reads the clicked cadence to live-update prices and readout, lays the plan cards out cleanly, and renders the rail on Home/Pricing/FAQ. The only files differing across reference/baseline/bad are src/scss/_planlever.scss, src/js/plan-billing.js, and src/pug/includes/planrail.pug. A shallow non-fix that only narrows the fixed rail row, moves the toggle pill without re-reading prices, shingles the cards, and forgets the FAQ route fails no_horizontal_overflow (tol 24px), visual_regression, cross-page dom_assertions, and interaction_assertions together.

Its Pricing page hosts a genuine commercial control - a billing cadence toggle over three plan tiers plus a shared cross-page plan rail - which makes it an ideal native host for a repair/regression_continuity task with four orthogonal discriminators (mobile overflow, visual regression, cross-page DOM, and interaction trajectory).
